Žugić reportedly told the daily Dan that he did not act illegally and that aid to relatives of bank employees is not unprecedented. The source reports no finding on the claim.
cases.source_title: Sukob u vrhu Centralne banke Crne Gore (RFE/RL Balkan)

cases.people: Irena Radović (deputy governor for banking supervision)
cases.summary: In July 2018 the bank's Council, chaired by governor Radoje Žugić, reportedly found that deputy governor Irena Radović lacked the required expertise, put personal interest ahead of the public interest and disclosed business secrets, and the bank asked parliament to dismiss her. She called this retaliation for revealing secrets about the bank's operations, called the decision illegal and said she would sue. The findings come from an internal body in an open dispute and the source reports no court ruling on them.
cases.source_title: Sukob u vrhu Centralne banke Crne Gore (RFE/RL Balkan)

cases.people: Milo Djukanovic (prime minister); Igor Luksic (finance minister); Radoje Zugic (First Bank board member)
cases.summary: Claim, not confirmed: in July 2012 the NGO MANS filed reports with Special Prosecutor Djurdjina Ivanovic alleging that First Bank received a €44 million state loan in 2008 that it could not repay and €192.2 million from state stock sales in 2009. MANS also alleged that the accused changed banking laws and fired Central Bank administrators so the Central Bank could not supervise First Bank. These are an NGO's reports to the prosecutor; the source reports no charge brought by prosecutors.
cases.source_title: Montenegro: Corruption Charges Against Top Politicians, First Bank and Central Bank Officials (OCCRP)

cases.people: Papuna Lezhava, Archil Mestvrishvili, Nikoloz Gagua (vice presidents); Giorgi Bakradze (advisor to the president); Natia Turnava (acting president, who did not resign)
cases.summary: The National Bank unfroze assets tied to Otar Partskhaladze, a former Prosecutor General sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury, arguing that Georgian citizens cannot be sanctioned without a Georgian court conviction. Three of its four vice presidents and an advisor submitted resignations over the decision. President Salome Zurabishvili criticized acting president Natia Turnava for reportedly changing the rules unilaterally; the source cites no court verdict or official finding.
cases.source_title: Top Georgian central bank officials resign over unfreezing of assets of sanctioned former prosecutor (bne IntelliNews)
cases.update_title: Scandal around ex-general prosecutor continues in Georgia; Vice-presidents leave the National Bank (JAMnews, 20 Sep 2023)

cases.people: Nana Keinishvili (National Bank Council member)
cases.summary: Georgia's Prosecutor's Office is investigating Council member Nana Keinishvili for possible unlawful involvement in business activities by a public official, after complaints from the management of crypto firm Bitexchange LLC, which the National Bank forwarded. The bank had fined Bitexchange; RFE/RL reported the fine at 572 million lari, and the bank did not disclose the amount. The investigation was ongoing as of October 2026.
cases.source_title: Georgia's Prosecutor's Office launches investigation into National Bank Council member (JAMnews)

cases.central_bank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
cases.people: Senad Softić (governor)
cases.summary: A criminal complaint accused governor Senad Softić of suspected wrongdoing in several cases, including a project to acquire an office building in Pale and a procedure to buy land in Sarajevo. The BiH Prosecutor's Office said in February 2023 that it had opened a case and was verifying the allegations. The central bank said examining allegations is not an investigation and that reports of one were untrue.
cases.source_title: Bosnia examining criminal complaints against c-bank governor (SeeNews)

cases.people: N. Zoljargal (former governor)
cases.summary: The anti-corruption agency IAAC arrested former governor N. Zoljargal on 29 November 2017 and said the case concerned the "Chinggis bond" and a price stabilizing programme, as part of a probe into the bank's 2012-2016 administration. A court released him with a travel ban, and prosecutors had not officially charged him. No later outcome was found.
cases.source_title: Former chief of Mongolia's Central Bank released on bail (News.MN)

cases.people: N. Zoljargal (central bank president)
cases.summary: News.MN reported in April 2020 that N. Zoljargal, then president of the central bank, was charged along with former MP B. Bolor and MPs D. Ganbat and D. Erdenebat with abuse of power over illegally transferring 49 percent of the Erdenet Mining Company. The source gives no outcome, and none was found.
cases.source_title: Q1 2020 case review, published 8 April 2020 (News.MN)

cases.central_bank: National Bank of the Republic of Belarus
cases.people: head of the main directorate for currency and financial monitoring and his deputy (roles only)
cases.summary: Belarus's KGB said in December 2016 that a directorate head at the National Bank and his deputy were arrested over a bribe, reported as 13,000 dollars, for choosing the company BelAVM as an equipment supplier. The bribes were allegedly paid in October and November 2016 through intermediaries. The source reports arrests only, with no charges beyond that or a verdict.
cases.source_title: В Белоруссии раскрыли коррупционную сеть, созданную поставщиками компьютерной техники (MK)

cases.people: Abdelwahab Keramane (former governor)
cases.summary: In the Khalifa Bank case, the Blida criminal court sentenced former governor Abdelwahab Keramane in absentia to 20 years in prison in 2007. On 7 June 2022 the Blida criminal court acquitted him. The pages opened do not state the specific charges.
cases.source_title: Abdelmoumene Khalifa condamné à 18 ans de prison, huit autres accusés acquittés (Algérie Eco)

cases.people: Mohammad Al Hashel (governor)
cases.summary: Claim, not confirmed: the Kuwaiti newspaper Al Jarida, citing unnamed sources, reported that the securities regulator had decided to refer Governor Mohammad Al Hashel to prosecutors for suspected breach of investment rules over shares in a local bank. He denied it, saying he had never traded shares in a listed company during his senior posts and that buying 2,172 shares in a capital increase did not use inside information. The regulator did not answer Reuters' calls and the article reports no outcome.
cases.source_title: Kuwait central bank chief denies illicit share trading (Gulf News)

cases.people: two convicted persons (unnamed in source)
cases.summary: The Misrata Criminal Court convicted two people of belonging to an organization set up to seize US$128 million and €5 million from the central bank's Sirte branch in 2013 through coercion. One got 15 years in prison and a LD 2.5 million fine; the other got 13 years and a LD 50,000 fine. The Attorney General's Office reported the ruling in October 2023.
cases.source_title: Two convicted for stealing Central Bank of Libya funds worth over US$ 128 million (Libya Herald)

cases.people: Saddek Elkaber (governor)
cases.summary: Global Witness reported that most Libyan letters of credit enter the international system through ABC International Bank in London, a commercial bank indirectly owned by the central bank and chaired by Governor Saddek Elkaber. It called this a clear conflict of interest, given his authority over letters of credit and anti-money-laundering rules. It built a database of nearly $2.5bn of letters of credit over 13 weeks in 2020 and said sources described mispricing, laundering and procurement fraud; the page reports no official finding of fraud.
cases.source_title: Global Witness reveals fraudulent Libyan Letters of Credit money entering international financial system via London (Global Witness)

cases.people: Ali al-Hibri (deputy governor); Saddek Elkaber (governor, complainant)
cases.summary: In November 2022 the central bank accused its deputy governor, Ali al-Hibri, of signing forged 50-dinar banknotes it said were printed in Russia and bore his signature, and Governor Saddek Elkaber asked the Attorney-General to pursue a complaint. The bank did not say how many notes were involved. The article gives no response from al-Hibri and no later outcome.
cases.source_title: CBL governor files legal complaint against his deputy over forged banknotes (Libya Update)

cases.people: staff (none named or mentioned in source)
cases.summary: Bank Al-Maghrib said on 4 July 2019 that 1.2 million dirhams ($125,000) was stolen during a movement of cash from the Dar As-Sikkah mint to cities in northern Morocco. The bank called it an isolated but malicious act and opened an investigation; the page reports no findings or arrests.
cases.source_title: Moroccan central bank opens investigation into stolen cash (Central Banking)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: Bank Al-Maghrib filed a complaint with the prosecutor's office against one of its staff and a service provider over suspected corruption in awarding contracts, after an internal investigation under its anti-corruption system. The article gives no amounts and no charges or ruling.
cases.source_title: BAM porte plainte contre un agent et un prestataire pour soupçons de corruption (Hespress)

cases.people: bank employee and others (names left out; pretrial suspects, no verdict found)
cases.summary: In July 2020 police under the Nouakchott-Ouest prosecutor arrested six people, including one bank employee, over foreign currency taken from the central bank; early reports said about $1 million and later reports $2.4 million, plus $500,000 in counterfeit notes. By March 2021 seven people were in pretrial detention, presumed to have taken about $1 million, and supporters held a sit-in demanding a quick trial. The pages opened report no trial or verdict.
cases.source_title: Mauritanie: six présumés voleurs du million de dollars à la Banque centrale arrêtés (Le360 Afrique)

cases.central_bank: Banque de la République du Burundi
cases.people: Dieudonné Murengerantwari (governor)
cases.summary: In October 2023 the Ministry of Justice said dismissed governor Dieudonné Murengerantwari was being prosecuted for passive corruption, money laundering, misappropriation of public property and undermining the national economy. The prosecutor called this description of the facts provisional, and he was being questioned at the time of the report.
cases.source_title: Burundi: Central Bank governor prosecuted for corruption (Africanews)

cases.people: Deogratias Mutombo (governor, 2013-2021)
cases.summary: An April 2021 report by Congo's IGF finance inspectorate called a 43 million USD transfer from a central bank account at BGFI Bank to food importer Egal an embezzlement of public funds, and said the bank kept false accounts to cover it. The bank's 2013 accounts showed about 43.1 million USD in that account when the real balance was about 119,000 USD. Mutombo, the bank and PwC did not respond to the journalists who reported this from leaked BGFI documents.
cases.source_title: Congo Hold-up : la caisse noire de la Banque centrale du Congo (Seneweb)

cases.people: Deogratias Mutombo (former governor)
cases.summary: Belgium's federal prosecutor opened a money laundering investigation into former governor Deogratias Mutombo and five others over hundreds of thousands of dollars allegedly moved through Belgium from DR Congo, with searches in September 2023. As of October 2024 the prosecutor said no suspect had been charged.
cases.source_title: Soupçons de blanchiment : la justice belge enquête sur l'ex-patron de la Banque centrale du Congo (Orishas Finance)

cases.people: Amadou Colley (governor)
cases.summary: The Janneh Commission found that governor Amadou Colley let former President Jammeh and General Sulayman Badjie withdraw funds without proper authorization, including millions of dollars by Badjie. A government White Paper banned Colley from public office for life and held him jointly liable for the money withdrawn in breach of the bank's procedures.
cases.source_title: Former CBG Governor Amadou Colley Banned From Holding Public Office For Life (Africa-Press)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: In March 2008 Ethiopian anti-corruption officials arrested 26 people after 90 kilos of fake gold were found in the central bank's vaults. Seven of those held were from the National Bank of Ethiopia, four from the Ethiopian Geological Survey and 15 were businessmen and collaborators. The report covers arrests only, not charges or court outcomes.
cases.source_title: Ethiopia makes arrests over fake gold scandal (Central Banking)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: The National Bank of Rwanda lost Rwf63 million from deposit accounts in early 2014 in a fraud reported to involve bank staff. The bank's ICT director said the suspects manipulated its internal security system before taking the cash. One person was arrested and the file sent to the Prosecutor General, while police said the prime suspect was believed to have fled to Uganda.
cases.source_title: Workers defraud central bank of Rwf63m, prime suspect on the run (The New Times)

cases.people: Bank of Zambia section officer (named in the source)
cases.summary: In October 2015 Zambia's Drug Enforcement Commission arrested Bank of Zambia a section officer for theft by a public servant and money laundering. He was accused of taking USD 43,660 and K20,335 in cash from his employer between January and September 2015. The report gives no court outcome.
cases.source_title: DEC arrests money laundering BoZ employee (QFM Zambia)

cases.people: Ernesto Gove (governor); Silvia de Abreu (board member)
cases.summary: Letters from 2013 presented in a US trial showed the Bank of Mozambique authorized Proindicus to seek a $372 million Credit Suisse loan, later $622 million, and Ematum an $850 million loan, part of the 'hidden debts' of over $2 billion. The letters were signed by board member Silvia de Abreu after a dispatch from governor Ernesto Gove, who in 2016 denied responsibility and said he had never heard of Proindicus. The newssheet Carta de Moçambique reported Gove's suspect status was confirmed and that he may face charges of abuse of office and membership of a criminal organisation.
cases.source_title: Bank of Mozambique involved in hidden debts – AIM report (Club of Mozambique)

cases.people: Ernesto Gove (former governor); board members (unnamed)
cases.summary: In April 2023 the daily Noticias, citing judicial sources, reported that former governor Ernesto Gove and two other central bank board members were among four accused in a second hidden debts trial being prepared. No trial date had been set, and the report lists no specific charges. Follow-up to the earlier record on the same case; no later outcome was confirmed in this search.
cases.source_title: Hidden debts: second trial under preparation (Club of Mozambique)

cases.people: former Deputy Governor (unnamed in source)
cases.summary: Final findings of Bhutan's Anti-Corruption Commission said a former Deputy Governor of the Royal Monetary Authority allegedly forged official documents, misused power and concealed earnings from World Bank and Asian Development Bank projects. An anonymous informer raised the case in October 2014. The case was forwarded to the Office of the Attorney General; the report gives no later outcome.
cases.source_title: RMA's former Deputy Governor allegedly forged official documents and misused power, says ACC findings (BBS)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: A former currency-exchange employee at the Bank of Korea's Daejeon Sejong-Chungnam headquarters broke the first-in, first-out rule at a coin collector's request, letting 240,000 100-won coins from 2018-2019 be issued before 2017 coins. The collector earned about 180 million won selling the coins and gave the employee about 55 million won. The Daejeon District Court sentenced the employee to 2 years 6 months in prison, a 1 million won fine and confiscation of about 43.31 million won.
cases.source_title: "Rare Coins Are Valuable"... Former Bank of Korea Employee Sentenced for Embezzling Coins (Asia Economy)

cases.people: news media staff (unnamed), not Reserve Bank staff
cases.summary: Information on the March Official Cash Rate cut was shared from the bank's media lock-up on 10 March and passed to an economics blogger before the official release. An independent investigation by Deloitte's forensic unit traced the leak to a Newshub Mediaworks reporter. The Reserve Bank ended embargoed lock-ups for news media and analysts.
cases.source_title: Reserve Bank takes action after investigation confirms leak (Reserve Bank of New Zealand)

cases.people: Rerngchai Marakanond (former governor)
cases.summary: A case was brought in 2001 after former governor Rerngchai Marakanond, among other policy-makers, decided to use the central bank's reserves to defend the baht during the Asian financial crisis. On October 5, 2016 Thailand's Supreme Court upheld a lower court's ruling that he had not acted improperly, closing the 15-year case.
cases.source_title: Former Bank of Thailand governor cleared of Asian financial crisis charges (Central Banking)

cases.people: Senior Exchange Control Officer (named in the source)
cases.summary: A Senior Exchange Control Officer at the National Reserve Bank of Tonga forged a Government bond to support another person's New Zealand visa application and asked for $2,500 pa'anga. She pleaded guilty to forgery, knowingly dealing with forged documents and obtaining money by false pretenses, and her employment was terminated. On May 21, 2019 the Supreme Court of Tonga gave her a two-year sentence, fully suspended, and ordered $800 compensation.
cases.source_title: Former Reserve Bank officer gets suspended sentence for serious fraud (Matangi Tonga)

cases.people: board of directors (as a group)
cases.summary: Tonga's Anti-Corruption Commissioner sued the bank and its directors, alleging that a 2024 staff payment (for example $6,600 to each of 73 staff) was an unlawful bonus linked to record profit, a breach of trust and misfeasance in public office. The board had described it as a one-off anniversary payout. On 20 November 2025 the Court of Appeal dismissed the proceedings, finding no reasonable cause of action against the bank and that the claim against the directors also failed.
cases.source_title: National Reserve Bank of Tonga v Anti-Corruption Commissioner [2025] TOCA 25 (Court of Appeal of Tonga, PacLII)

cases.people: BSP bank examiner (named in the source)
cases.summary: After auditing the Rural Bank of Sapang Dalaga in late 2005, a BSP examiner took consultancy fees from the bank through a third-party firm, collecting P5,000 monthly for a total of P103,500. The court found he used false pretenses and threatened BSP sanctions. The Sandiganbayan denied his appeal and affirmed the guilty verdict, with six years and one month to seven years in prison and perpetual disqualification from public office.
cases.source_title: Sandiganbayan upholds conviction of ex-BSP examiner (BusinessWorld)

cases.people: Former officer, BSP Supervision and Examination Sector (named in the source)
cases.summary: A former officer of the BSP's Supervision and Examination Sector obtained a loan from the Rural Bank of Kiamba, Sarangani, Inc. in 2006. The Ombudsman cleared him in 2011 of liability under Section 27(d) in relation to Section 36 of Republic Act 7653. On a petition by the BSP, the Supreme Court reversed the Ombudsman and ordered the filing of criminal charges; the report does not say whether they have been filed.
cases.source_title: SC orders filing of charges vs former BSP exec (Manila Times)

cases.people: Manager, BSP Bacolod office (named in the source)
cases.summary: BSP's internal audit reviewed cash at the Bacolod City branch, spotted thinner-than-standard bundles of P500 bills and found a shortfall of P5.955 million. In an affidavit, the branch manager reportedly said he used the money for lending and "treasure hunting". The Ombudsman found him guilty of dishonesty, ordered his dismissal with forfeiture of benefits, and was set to file malversation charges.
cases.source_title: Ombudsman orders dismissal of BSP exec (Philippine Star)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: A BSP legal department investigation that began in November 2023 found four staff had falsified attendance records; they were dismissed in July 2024. In August 2025 the Monetary Board approved the maximum administrative penalties for two supervisors found involved in falsifying those records, including dismissal, forfeiture of retirement benefits and perpetual disqualification from public office.
cases.source_title: BSP hammer drops on bosses in 'ghost employee' scandal (Manila Bulletin)

cases.people: Benjamin Diokno (BSP Governor); six other BSP officials
cases.summary: In January 2021 the chairman of Stop Corruption Organization of the Philippines filed a graft complaint at the Ombudsman against Governor Benjamin Diokno and six other BSP officials over a P1.75-billion national ID card contract awarded to AllCard International. He alleged the bidding terms required buying materials from OVD Kinegram AG without separate public bidding. These are the complainant's allegations; the report gives no finding.
cases.source_title: Diokno, 6 other BSP execs sued over national ID deal (Philippine Star)

cases.people: Amando Tetangco Jr. (former BSP governor and Monetary Board chairman); Monetary Board members
cases.summary: A 2013 graft complaint at the Ombudsman, filed by Joselito Yujuico and others tied to GenBank, says former governor Amando Tetangco Jr., Monetary Board members and other officials caused undue injury and gave undue advantage to Allied Bank by allowing its merger with Philippine National Bank on February 9, 2013. In September 2025 the complaint was reported still pending, and the complainants asked for an immediate resolution.
cases.source_title: Ombudsman urged to resolve graft raps vs former BSP-MB execs (Malaya)

cases.people: Joseph Yam Chi-kwong (former HKMA chief)
cases.summary: A Legislative Council subcommittee report said former HKMA chief Joseph Yam Chi-kwong should bear "ultimate responsibility" for investors' losses from irregularities in Lehman's minibonds and structured products, because he headed the banking watchdog at the time. The HKMA replied that the report had not fully taken into account the information it submitted, and some members prepared a minority report.
cases.source_title: Lehman criticism played down (South China Morning Post)
cases.update_title: HKMA statement on the subcommittee report, 6 June 2012 (HKMA)

revolving_door.people: Philipp Hildebrand (chairman of the SNB governing board until January 2012)

revolving_door.source_title: Philipp Hildebrand, Vice Chairman (BlackRock)
revolving_door.move: from Swiss National Bank chairman to vice chairman of asset manager BlackRock

revolving_door.move: from vice chairman and managing director of Goldman Sachs International (2002-2005) to Banca d'Italia governor

revolving_door.move: from Senior European Economist at Goldman Sachs to external Monetary Policy Committee member, then Deputy Governor

revolving_door.source_title: Ben Broadbent (Bank of England)

revolving_door.summary: The Bank of England's biography states Michael Saunders was UK economist at Citigroup from 1990 to 2016, having joined Salomon Brothers, which became part of Citi by merger, and was an economist at Greenwell Montagu (now part of HSBC) from 1988 to 1990. He was an external Monetary Policy Committee member from 9 August 2016 to 8 August 2022.
revolving_door.source_title: Michael Saunders (Bank of England)

revolving_door.move: from Chief UK Economist at Morgan Stanley to Monetary Policy Committee member
revolving_door.summary: The Bank of England's biography states David Miles was Chief UK Economist at Morgan Stanley from October 2004 to May 2009. He was a Monetary Policy Committee member from 2009 until 2015.

revolving_door.source_title: Kristin Forbes (Bank of England)

revolving_door.summary: A Bloomberg report carried by Gulf News, citing the Financial Times, says Mervyn King joined Citigroup Inc as a senior adviser in April. It says he retired from the Bank of England in 2013 after a decade overseeing UK monetary policy.
revolving_door.source_title: Citigroup hires former Bank of England Governor King (Gulf News / Bloomberg)

revolving_door.move: from Chief Executive Officer of Investec Bank plc and co-founder of Grovepoint Capital LLP to Chair of the Bank of England's Court
revolving_door.summary: The Bank of England's biography states Bradley Fried is a co-founder of Grovepoint Capital LLP, prior to which he was Chief Executive Officer of Investec Bank plc, which he joined in 1999. He was appointed Chair of Court effective 1 July 2018, with a term to 30 June 2022.
revolving_door.source_title: Bradley Fried (Bank of England)

revolving_door.move: from executive and chair roles at Barclays, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, Beazley and Bawag to Chair of the Bank of England's Court

His second four-year term as Chair of Court starts on 24 October 2026.
revolving_door.source_title: David Roberts reappointed as Chair of the Bank of England's Court of Directors (Bank of England)

revolving_door.move: from investing at Apax Partners and co-founding Amadeus Capital Partners to Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court
revolving_door.summary: The Bank of England states Dame Anne Glover is Chief Executive and Co-Founder of Amadeus Capital Partners, and that her career includes investing at Apax Partners. She was reappointed as a Non-Executive Director of Court until 31 May 2028.
revolving_door.source_title: David Roberts reappointed as Chair of the Bank of England's Court of Directors (Bank of England)

revolving_door.people: Diana Noble (Non-Executive Director and Deputy Chair, Court)

She was reappointed as a Non-Executive Director of Court until 31 May 2027.
revolving_door.source_title: David Roberts reappointed as Chair of the Bank of England's Court of Directors (Bank of England)

revolving_door.move: from investment banking at Blackstone, Barclays Capital, ABN AMRO and Baring Brothers to Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court
revolving_door.summary: The Bank of England states Lord Jitesh Gadhia has over 25 years in investment banking and financial services, with senior positions at Blackstone, Barclays Capital, ABN AMRO and Baring Brothers. He was reappointed to Court for a second four-year term beginning 24 October 2026.
revolving_door.source_title: Chancellor announces Bank of England appointments (Bank of England)

revolving_door.people: Hanneke Smits (Non-Executive Director, Court, from 1 January 2027)
revolving_door.move: from Global Head of BNY Investment Management to Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court
revolving_door.summary: The Bank of England states Hanneke Smits was Global Head of BNY Investment Management and a member of BNY's Executive Committee. Her four-year term on Court begins on 1 January 2027.
revolving_door.source_title: Chancellor announces Bank of England appointments (Bank of England)

revolving_door.move: from non-executive role at Unity Trust Bank to Non-Executive Director of the Bank of England's Court

revolving_door.source_title: Neel Kashkari (Federal Reserve History)
